correctness.rationale: The nonzero states split into \(k\) phase classes, and every transition that avoids the sink advances phase by one. Thus a word of rank at most \(k-r\) must kill at least \(r+1\) phases. For a killed phase representative, entering the sink forces a full occurrence of \(u\); distinct killed phases force distinct starting residues modulo \(k\). Since \(u\) is unbordered, selected occurrences cannot overlap, and distinct residues exclude a start gap exactly divisible by \(k\), so consecutive starts are at least \(k+1\) apart. This gives the lower bound \(k+r(k+1)\). The first copy of \(u\) merges each surviving two-state phase to at most one image, while the \(r+1\) displayed copies in \(u(au)^r\) start in distinct residue classes and kill that many phases, giving the matching rank. A fresh independent power-automaton replay for all binary unbordered words through \(k=5\) reproduced the threshold sequence, and the frozen verifier extends exact BFS checks to binary \(k\le7\) and ternary \(k\le5\); these finite checks are corroborative only.
